programmes.name_local: DOST-PCIEERD Research and Development / Technology Transfer Funding
programmes.name_en: DOST-PCIEERD R&D and Technology Transfer Funding
programmes.funder: Philippine Council for Industry, Energy and Emerging Technology Research and Development (DOST-PCIEERD)
programmes.amount_note: Competitive R&D and technology transfer funding across industry, energy and emerging technology sectors, including programmes such as the Technology Business Incubation support, CRADLE (collaborative R&D with industry) and Startup Research grants. Awards range widely with the project scope.
programmes.deadline_note: PCIEERD issues multiple calls per year across its programmes, each with its own deadline published on the PCIEERD website.
programmes.reopen_note: PCIEERD calls recur annually. Subscribe to PCIEERD announcements to catch the CRADLE, Startup Research and technology transfer calls, which have different timings.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify the relevant PCIEERD programme and open call.
For CRADLE-type calls, secure a partner higher education institution or research institution.
Submit the proposal through the DOST Project Management Information System.
Memorandum of agreement and fund release.

eligibility.other_note: Philippine-registered companies, higher education institutions and research organisations. Industry-partnered calls require a company to shoulder a share of the project cost.

programmes.source_snippet: DOST-PCIEERD funds research and development and technology transfer in the industry, energy and emerging technology sectors.

programmes.funder: Department of Science and Technology (DOST), Philippines
programmes.amount_note: Grants under the Innovative Startup Act (Republic Act 11337) for startup development, prototyping and commercialisation. Award sizes vary by call and by implementing DOST council, historically ranging from several hundred thousand to a few million pesos.
programmes.deadline_note: Runs in calls announced by DOST and its councils (notably PCIEERD), typically with windows of four to eight weeks.
programmes.reopen_note: The Startup Grant Fund is a standing facility under the Innovative Startup Act with recurring calls funded from the annual national budget. Monitor startupgrantfund.dost.gov.ph and PCIEERD announcements for the next call.

procedure_steps.detail: Register on the DOST Startup Grant Fund portal.
Submit the proposal with the technology description, market validation and budget.
Technical and financial evaluation by DOST panels.
Memorandum of agreement and milestone-based release of funds.

documents_required.doc: Audited financial statements or statement of assets
Endorsement from a host institution where required

eligibility.other_note: Philippine-registered startups and startup enablers as defined in Republic Act 11337 (the Innovative Startup Act), generally majority Filipino-owned and registered for not more than five years.

programmes.source_snippet: The Startup Grant Fund supports Philippine startups and startup enablers under the Innovative Startup Act.

programmes.name_local: DTI Shared Service Facilities and Negosyo Center support
programmes.name_en: DTI Shared Service Facilities and Negosyo Center Support
programmes.amount_note: Provision of shared production equipment and facilities to MSME cooperatives and associations, plus free business advisory, registration assistance and training through the nationwide Negosyo Center network. No cash grant to individual founders.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling. Negosyo Centers operate continuously; Shared Service Facility proposals are assessed by regional DTI offices as budget allows.

procedure_steps.detail: Visit the nearest Negosyo Center for advisory and registration assistance.
For Shared Service Facilities, a cooperative, association or LGU submits a proposal to the DTI regional office.
DTI assessment of the industry cluster need.
Equipment procurement and deployment to the cooperator.

documents_required.doc: Proposal and beneficiary list (for Shared Service Facilities)

eligibility.other_note: Philippine micro, small and medium enterprises. Shared Service Facilities are awarded to cooperators (cooperatives, associations, LGUs, academic institutions) serving groups of MSMEs rather than to individual firms.

programmes.source_snippet: Negosyo Centers provide business registration assistance, advisory services and training to Philippine MSMEs.

programmes.funder: Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) with the National Development Company (NDC)
programmes.amount_note: A government equity co-investment vehicle established under the Innovative Startup Act to invest in Philippine startups alongside private investors. Investment amounts are deal-specific and the fund invests rather than granting.
programmes.deadline_note: No public application round. The fund invests through the National Development Company and partner fund managers; deployment activity has been limited and intermittent since establishment.
programmes.reopen_note: Deployment of the Startup Venture Fund has depended on annual appropriations under the Innovative Startup Act. Confirm the fund's current investment activity with DTI or NDC before relying on it; in practice most Philippine startups raise from private VCs and the QBO and IdeaSpace ecosystems.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact DTI's Competitiveness and Innovation Group or the National Development Company to confirm current activity.
Where active, submit the investment proposal.

eligibility.other_note: Philippine-registered startups qualifying under the Innovative Startup Act. Exact investment criteria are not publicly detailed.

programmes.source_snippet: The Startup Venture Fund was created under Republic Act 11337 to invest in Philippine startups.
